t: The lands of central Italy ruled by the popes as temporal sovereigns from the Frankish donations of the 750s until 1870.
Papal control was often weak, but Renaissance popes made the state a real power and Rome an artistic capital.
Napoleon and then Italian unification dismantled it; Vatican City, created in 1929, is its last remnant.
dyk: Pope Julius II, who founded the Swiss Guard in 1506, personally led his army in winter 1511 and entered the captured town of Mirandola through a breach in its walls.
ev: Pope Stephen II wins the protection of Pepin the Short against the Lombards
Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor in Rome
Cardinal Albornoz issues the Egidian Constitutions
Julius II takes Bologna and founds the Swiss Guard
Napoleon annexes the Papal States to the French Empire
Defeat at Castelfidardo; the Marche and Umbria join Italy
Italian troops enter Rome through the breach at Porta Pia

f.founder: Pope Stephen II, with Pepin the Short
f.predecessor: Byzantine Empire (Duchy of Rome and Exarchate of Ravenna)
